title: CIMFlow: An Integrated Framework for Systematic Design and Evaluation of Digital CIM Architectures
problem: Digital compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures promise DNN acceleration by addressing the memory wall, but lack comprehensive design and evaluation frameworks that cover both software (compilation) and hardware design spaces, and fail to address capacity constraints inherent in CIM systems.
motivation: CIM is a promising paradigm for energy-efficient DNN acceleration, but design complexity and evaluation challenges limit adoption and optimization.
method: CIMFlow is an integrated framework providing end-to-end workflow for implementing and evaluating DNN workloads on digital CIM. It bridges compilation and simulation infrastructures with flexible instruction set architecture (ISA) design. The framework addresses CIM capacity constraints through advanced partitioning and parallelism strategies in the compilation flow.
key_novelty: Unified framework bridging compilation and simulation with advanced partitioning strategies specifically addressing digital CIM capacity constraints.
contributions: Out-of-the-box CIMFlow workflow for DNN implementation and evaluation
Flexible ISA design connecting compilation and simulation
Advanced partitioning and parallelism strategies handling CIM capacity constraints

metrics.other: enables systematic design space exploration of digital CIM architectures

limitations: Framework paper; specific performance metrics and comparison results not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: integrated framework for digital CIM design and optimization
